questions.stem: When analysing a German text, what do the letters PACT stand for?
options: Purpose, audience, context and tone
Plot, argument, character and theme
Persuasion, analysis, content and title
Purpose, argument, conclusion and text type
questions.explanation: PACT asks why the text was written, who it is for, the situation it comes from, and the attitude or mood its language creates.

questions.stem: 'Hey Leute! Am Samstag steigt unser Sommerfest im Jugendzentrum, mit DJ, Grillen und Tischtennisturnier. Bringt eure Freunde mit!' Who is the audience?
options: Parents who must sign a permission form
Local businesses who are being asked to sponsor the event
Teachers organising the end-of-year exams
Young people who might come to the youth centre
questions.explanation: 'Hey Leute', the 'ihr' forms ('Bringt eure Freunde mit') and the slang 'steigt' (is happening) address young people informally. Nothing addresses parents or sponsors.

questions.stem: 'Sehr geehrte Anwohnerinnen und Anwohner, wegen Bauarbeiten ist die Lindenstraße vom 3. bis 14. Juni gesperrt. Wir bitten um Ihr Verständnis.' What is the main purpose?
options: To persuade residents to protest the works
To apologise for damage to residents' homes
To invite residents to a street party
To inform residents about a road closure
questions.explanation: The notice gives the facts of a closure (where, when, why). 'Wir bitten um Ihr Verständnis' is a polite formula asking for understanding, not an apology for damage.

questions.stem: 'Na toll. Schon wieder fällt der Bus aus. Wirklich super, liebe Verkehrsbetriebe!' What is the tone?
options: Worried and fearful
Sarcastic and annoyed
Grateful and relieved
Neutral and factual
questions.explanation: 'Na toll' and 'wirklich super' say the opposite of what is meant, after a complaint that the bus is cancelled again ('schon wieder'). The praise is sarcastic.

questions.stem: 'Liebe Oma, vielen Dank für das Paket! Deine Kekse haben meine erste Prüfungswoche gerettet.' What context can you infer?
options: A grandchild writing during exams after a parcel came
A grandmother thanking a bakery for an order
A student writing to a teacher about a test
A company thanking a regular customer for a recent purchase
questions.explanation: 'Liebe Oma' and 'deine' show an informal family relationship, and 'meine erste Prüfungswoche' places the writer in an exam period. The parcel came from the grandmother.

questions.stem: Which feature most clearly signals a formal register in a German text?
options: Exclamations such as 'Krass!'
'Sie' and 'Ihnen' used throughout
Frequent use of 'du' and 'euch'
Abbreviations such as 'LG' and 'hdl'
questions.explanation: The polite pronouns 'Sie', 'Ihnen' and 'Ihr' mark formal address. 'Du' forms, chat abbreviations and slang exclamations all signal an informal register.

questions.stem: 'Wusstest du, wie viele Stunden du jede Woche am Handy verbringst? Zeit, etwas zu ändern!' What is the main purpose?
options: To entertain readers with a story about phones
To advertise a new smartphone to teenagers
To persuade readers to change their phone habits
To report the results of a scientific study
questions.explanation: A rhetorical question addressed to the reader, followed by a call to action ('Zeit, etwas zu ändern!'), shows a persuasive purpose. No study or product is mentioned.

questions.stem: A question asks you to identify the tone of a German text and justify your answer. What makes a strong answer?
options: Naming the tone and citing the words in the text that create it
Summarising the whole text in your own words
Giving your own opinion about the topic the text deals with, in detail
Translating the whole text into English
questions.explanation: Justifying means supporting the claim with evidence: quote or refer to specific words, such as sarcastic praise or a rhetorical question, and explain their effect.

questions.stem: 'Der Artikel nennt nur die Vorteile von Ganztagsschulen; Kritiker kommen nicht zu Wort.' What would an evaluation of the article conclude?
options: It is unreliable, because it is written in German
It is one-sided, because opposing views are left out
It is balanced, because it reports a range of views
It is objective, because it appears in a newspaper
questions.explanation: 'Kritiker kommen nicht zu Wort' means critics do not get a say. An article giving only the advantages is one-sided; appearing in a newspaper does not make it objective.

questions.stem: A task asks for a blog post in German addressing three bullet points. How is it best organised?
options: A short introduction, a paragraph per bullet point, then a conclusion
Only the bullet point you know most about, in detail
One long paragraph mixing all three points together
The three points set out as headings followed by notes, not full sentences
questions.explanation: Each bullet point is a required focus, so each deserves its own developed paragraph, framed by an opening and an ending that suit the text type. Notes without full sentences do not meet the task.

questions.stem: Which closing suits an informal email to a friend?
options: 'Viele liebe Grüße, deine Lena'
'Hochachtungsvoll, Lena Fischer'
'Mit freundlichen Grüßen, Lena Fischer'
'Sehr geehrte Lena'
questions.explanation: Informal emails end with phrases such as 'Viele Grüße', 'Liebe Grüße' or 'Bis bald' and 'dein' or 'deine' before the first name. 'Hochachtungsvoll' is very formal and old-fashioned.

questions.stem: You write an email to a teacher you know well, Herr Braun. Which greeting suits a friendly but respectful tone?
options: 'Sehr geehrter Braun,'
'Lieber Herr Braun,'
'Lieber Braun,'
'Hallo Braun!'
questions.explanation: 'Lieber' or 'Liebe' with the title and surname is warm but still respectful. A surname without 'Herr' or 'Frau' sounds rude in a greeting.

questions.stem: Why is the greeting in a German letter or email usually followed by a comma rather than an exclamation mark?
options: An exclamation mark is only used when writing to children
A comma shows the reader that the letter is formal rather than a casual note
An exclamation mark would make the greeting into a question
A comma is the modern convention, and the letter then starts in lower case
questions.explanation: Modern German letters write 'Liebe Anna,' and continue on the next line with a lower-case letter unless the word is a noun. The comma is used in both formal and informal letters.

questions.stem: Which closing line suits the transcript of a speech?
options: 'Vielen Dank für Ihre Aufmerksamkeit!'
'Mit freundlichen Grüßen'
'Bis bald, dein Max'
'Siehe Anhang'
questions.explanation: A speech ends by thanking the listeners. The other phrases close letters and emails or point to an attachment.

questions.stem: In a text message, what does 'sz' stand for?
options: sehr zuverlässig
sag zu
schreib zurück
so zufrieden
questions.explanation: Young Germans shorten common phrases in messages: 'sz' asks the reader to write back. Such abbreviations belong only in informal texts between friends.

questions.stem: What does '8ung' mean in a text message?
options: acht Uhr
achtzehn
achtsam
Achtung!
questions.explanation: The digit 8 is read 'acht', so '8ung' spells 'Achtung' (watch out). The same idea lies behind '4U' for 'für dich'.

questions.stem: A friend ends a message with 'sTn'. What does it mean?
options: schönen Tag noch
sehr toll, nicht?
sag Tschüss noch
schon Termin notiert
questions.explanation: 'sTn' wishes the reader a nice rest of the day. Other common ones are 'brb' (bin gleich wieder da) and 'LG' (liebe Grüße).

questions.stem: Which sentence is correctly written?
options: 'Ich glaube dass sie, recht hat.'
'Ich glaube, dass sie recht hat.'
'Ich glaube dass, sie recht hat.'
'Ich glaube, dass sie hat recht.'
questions.explanation: A comma always separates the main clause from a 'dass' clause, and it goes before 'dass'. In the subordinate clause the verb goes to the end.

questions.stem: Which sentence has the correct word order?
options: 'Meiner Meinung nach sollten wir mehr Rad fahren.'
'Meiner Meinung nach wir sollten mehr Rad fahren.'
'Meiner Meinung nach, wir sollten mehr Rad fahren.'
'Meiner Meinung nach wir mehr Rad fahren sollten.'
questions.explanation: 'Meiner Meinung nach' fills the first position, so the verb comes second, before the subject. No comma follows it, unlike 'In my opinion,' in English.

questions.stem: Which completes 'Ich bin überzeugt, dass ___.'?
options: 'lohnt sich ein Auslandsjahr'
'sich ein Auslandsjahr lohnt'
'sich lohnt ein Auslandsjahr'
'ein Auslandsjahr lohnt sich'
questions.explanation: After 'dass' the finite verb goes last: 'dass sich ein Auslandsjahr lohnt'. Main-clause order is wrong after a subordinating conjunction.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correctly punctuated?
options: 'Der Film, den wir gesehen haben, war spannend.'
'Der Film den wir gesehen haben, war spannend.'
'Der Film, den wir gesehen haben war spannend.'
'Der Film den wir, gesehen haben war spannend.'
questions.explanation: A relative clause in the middle of a sentence is enclosed by two commas, one before the relative pronoun and one after its verb.

questions.stem: Which words list three points in order in an argument?
options: erstens, zweitens, drittens
einmal, zweimal, dreimal
eins, zwei, drei
die erste, die zweite, die dritte
questions.explanation: Ordinal numbers with -ens act as linking adverbs: 'erstens ... zweitens ... drittens'. 'Einmal, zweimal' mean once, twice.

questions.stem: Which word completes 'Ich war sehr müde. ___ bin ich mit zur Party gegangen.'?
options: Trotzdem
Deshalb
Obwohl
Weil
questions.explanation: 'Trotzdem' ('nevertheless') links a contrast and, as an adverb, is followed by the verb. 'Obwohl' and 'weil' would send the verb to the end, and 'deshalb' makes no sense here.

questions.stem: Which pair completes '___ ist das Leben auf dem Land ruhig, ___ fahren dort kaum Busse.'?
options: Entweder ... oder
Weder ... noch
Sowohl ... als auch
Einerseits ... andererseits
questions.explanation: 'Einerseits ... andererseits' weighs one side against the other, and each is followed by the verb. 'Entweder ... oder' offers alternatives, which does not fit two facts.

questions.stem: What does 'Im Großen und Ganzen' mean at the start of a conclusion?
options: In great detail
By a large margin
In the long run
On the whole
questions.explanation: 'Im Großen und Ganzen' sums up an overall judgement, like 'im Allgemeinen'. 'In the long run' would be 'auf lange Sicht'.

questions.stem: What does 'Im Vergleich zu Australien beginnt die Schule in Deutschland früher am Morgen' do?
options: It concedes a point to the other side
It compares the two countries on one point
It contrasts two opinions about school
It gives a reason why school in Germany starts so early
questions.explanation: 'Im Vergleich zu' plus the dative ('compared with') introduces a comparison, which is useful when contrasting German-speaking and Australian experiences.

questions.stem: In a conversation you need a moment to think. Which is the most natural phrase?
options: 'Tja, das ist eine gute Frage ...'
'Ich verstehe nur Bahnhof.'
'Das ist mir Wurst.'
'Auf Wiederhören!'
questions.explanation: Fillers such as 'tja', 'also' and 'na ja' buy thinking time naturally. 'Ich verstehe nur Bahnhof' means you understand nothing, and 'Das ist mir Wurst' means you don't care.

questions.stem: Which sentence correctly begins a description of a picture stimulus?
options: 'Das Bild sieht man eine Gruppe Jugendlicher.'
'Auf dem Bild sieht man eine Gruppe Jugendlicher.'
'Im Bild sieht eine Gruppe Jugendlicher.'
'Auf dem Bild sieht man einer Gruppe Jugendlicher.'
questions.explanation: 'Auf dem Bild' (dative) locates what is shown, 'man' is the subject, and 'eine Gruppe' is the accusative object of 'sieht'. Without 'man' the sentence has no sensible subject.

questions.stem: The teacher asks 'Was würdest du an seiner Stelle machen?' What are you being asked?
options: What you would do in his position
What he did when he was in your position
Where you would go instead of him
Which job you would like to do later
questions.explanation: 'An seiner Stelle' means in his place, and 'würdest ... machen' asks for a hypothetical answer, best given in Konjunktiv II: 'An seiner Stelle würde ich ...'.

questions.stem: In the conversation you say 'Das erinnert mich an meinen Austausch in Hamburg.' What are you doing?
options: Summarising what the stimulus says
Linking the stimulus to a personal experience
Disagreeing politely with the teacher's opinion of the stimulus
Asking for the question to be repeated
questions.explanation: 'Das erinnert mich an' ('that reminds me of') connects the stimulus to your own experience, a good way to give a personal response and extend the conversation.

questions.stem: Asked 'Treibst du gern Sport?', which reply best keeps the conversation going?
options: 'Ja, ich spiele Hockey im Verein. Und du, was machst du gern?'
'Ja, ich spiele Hockey im Verein. Hockey, Hockey, Hockey.'
'Ja. Nein. Vielleicht. Ich weiß es wirklich überhaupt nicht.'
'Sport? Das ist eine Frage. Auf Wiedersehen und bis bald!'
questions.explanation: Giving a detail and then asking a question back keeps the exchange going. Repeating a word, or contradicting yourself and closing the conversation, shuts it down.

questions.stem: What is 'ein Bewerbungsschreiben'?
options: A table setting out one's schooling and work history
A letter applying for a job or training place
A written reference from a former employer
A contract signed on the first day of work
questions.explanation: The Bewerbungsschreiben (or Anschreiben) is the cover letter. A table of one's schooling and experience is the Lebenslauf, and a reference is an Arbeitszeugnis.

questions.stem: Which sentence suits the opening of a formal job application?
options: 'Lieber Chef, ich will unbedingt bei dir in der Firma arbeiten.'
'Mit großem Interesse habe ich Ihre Anzeige auf Ihrer Homepage gelesen.'
'Hi, ich habe eure Anzeige auf eurer Homepage gesehen, cool!'
'Na, wie geht's? Ich suche gerade einen Job bei einer Firma.'
questions.explanation: A formal application uses 'Sie' forms (Ihre Anzeige, Ihrer Homepage) and says where the advertisement was seen. 'Eure', 'dir', 'Hi' and 'Na' are far too casual.

questions.stem: In an application letter, what is 'Ich arbeite gern im Team und bin sehr zuverlässig' used for?
options: Asking for an interview at the end
Listing the documents that are enclosed
Describing one's strengths for the position
Saying where the job advertisement was seen
questions.explanation: The body of the letter explains why the applicant suits the job: strengths ('meine Stärken'), skills and experience. Asking for an interview comes in the closing lines.

questions.stem: What does 'Anlagen: Lebenslauf, Zeugnisse' at the end of an application mean?
options: The people who can give a reference
The places the applicant has worked
The documents enclosed with the letter
The plans the applicant has for the job
questions.explanation: 'Anlagen' (enclosures) lists what is sent with the letter, here a CV and school reports. It comes after the signature.

questions.stem: Which completes 'Ich bewerbe mich um einen Ausbildungsplatz als Mechatroniker, ___ ich mich schon lange für Technik interessiere.'?
options: denn
deshalb
trotzdem
da
questions.explanation: 'Da' ('since, as') is a subordinating conjunction, so the verb 'interessiere' at the end fits. 'Denn' would need main-clause order (denn ich interessiere mich), and the adverbs need the verb straight after them.
